new.n: Indian camp on the Black River, 1847 GLO plat
new.pl: East (left) bank of the Black River at the sec. 21/22 line, about 35.5 ch north of the 21/22/27/28 corner, T25N R2W, Clark County (1847 GLO plat and field notes)
new.v: Trade silver, beads, gun parts, kettle brass
new.st: The October 1847 government survey plat of T25N R2W marks an "Indian Camp" where the Black River crosses the line between secs. 21 and 22. The field notes for that line, run north from the 21/22/27/28 corner, set the right bank of the river at 31.18 chains and the left (east) bank meander post at 35.50 chains; the camp sat on the east bank there. At 1.30 chains on the line west between secs. 22 and 27 a road bore northwest. The notes do not name the camp itself, so the camp rests on the plat, placed by the measured river crossing.
new.t: Look at the east bank terrace by the sec. 21/22 line on the 1938 aerial and LiDAR. This is a native camp site: look only, take nothing, and ask the landowner before going on the ground.
new.warn: Native camp site: look only, take nothing.
